posts.text:
Friday, Nov 6: Toronto's streetcars lost 969 hours to delays, across all routes.

Hardest hit: 505 Dundas eastbound, where the typical trip lost 26 min (usually 23).
Smoothest: 507 Long Branch eastbound, 12 min.

#TTC #TransitSky #DataViz

https://stuckin.to/

Friday's slowest spot: Westbound on Fleet St, approaching Fort York Blvd.
The average streetcar lost 1 min 46 s here (usually 1 min 48 s). Across 297 trips, that adds up to 8.8 hours.
This signal has transit priority.
posts.alt: 3D map of Fleet St around Fort York Blvd, rotated to Toronto's street grid. Delay is drawn as a coloured ridge above the track, rising where streetcars lose time; the westbound stretch at Fort York Blvd is highlighted, peaking at about 1 min 46 s lost per streetcar.

shot.title: Fleet St westbound, approaching Fort York Blvd
shot.sub: Friday, Nov 6: 1 min 46 s lost per streetcar · 297 trips

posts.text:
Most short-turned, Friday, Nov 6: 505 Dundas. 1 in 7 trips (66) were sent back before the end of the line, most after Dundas St West at Lansdowne Ave (westbound, 29), instead of going on to Dundas West Station.

Across all routes, 5% of trips were short-turned.
posts.alt: Map of the 505 Dundas route in the waits view: a column at each stop, taller and darker where riders waited longer than scheduled, and yellow warning signs where cars were short-turned. A tooltip on the busiest spot, after Dundas St West at Lansdowne Ave, gives how many westbound cars were sent back there instead of going on to Dundas West Station.

posts.text:
Most held at a signal, Friday, Nov 6: eastbound at Fort York Blvd & Fleet St.

36% of streetcars waited 90 s or more beyond a clean approach, about a full signal cycle, despite transit priority.
About 299 streetcars came through.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Fort York Blvd & Fleet St, with arrows for each direction of streetcar travel into each signal, coloured by how often streetcars were held 90 seconds or more. A tooltip for the eastbound approach reads 36% held 90 s+, with a histogram of extra time through the approach.

posts.text:
Friday, Nov 6: at the busiest moment (5:10 pm), 151 streetcars were in service, against 151 scheduled.
Overall, 99% of scheduled streetcar service ran, and buses ran 1,048 hours on streetcar routes.
posts.alt: Line chart of streetcars in service through Friday, Nov 6, every 10 minutes from 4 am, against the TTC's schedule (dashed). The busiest moment was 151 streetcars at 5:10 pm, against 151 scheduled; over the day 99% of scheduled streetcar hours ran.

posts.text:
Longest extra wait at a stop, Friday, Nov 6: Broadview Ave at Gerrard St East (504 King westbound).

Riders waited 20.8 min on average, against 5.0 if cars had come as scheduled: 15.8 min extra. 1 in 7 cars came bunched, and 27 of 142 scheduled cars never came.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Broadview Ave at Gerrard St East in the waits view, a column at each stop. A tooltip for the stop reads 15.8 minutes of excess wait, with how often cars came bunched or with gaps, and a chart of the spread of gaps between cars.
